items.title: Specified finite GNS detailed balance

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §§1.2.4 and 1.3.4
Eric A. Carlen and Jan Maas, Gradient flow and entropy inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups with detailed balance, §2

items.statement:
Let $d\geq1$ be finite, let $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^d$ with its standard inner product, and write $M_d(\mathbb C)$ for its matrices. Let $H_{\rm s}=H_{\rm s}^*\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ be a Hamiltonian in joules, let $\hbar>0$ have units joule-seconds, and let $m\geq0$ be an integer with $L_1,\ldots,L_m\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ a finite family of jump matrices in seconds$^{-1/2}$. Matrices on which the generators act are dimensionless. The Schrödinger generator $\mathcal L$ is the finite GKSL generator of [[def-qsm-dt-gksl-definition]].

Its trace-dual observable generator is

$$G(A)=\frac{i}{\hbar}[H_{\rm s},A]+D(A),\qquad D(A)=\sum_{j=1}^{m}\left(L_j^*AL_j-\frac12\{L_j^*L_j,A\}\right).$$

Here $[U,V]=UV-VU$, $\{U,V\}=UV+VU$, and $A^*$ is the conjugate transpose. The units of $G$, $D$, and $\mathcal L$ are seconds$^{-1}$. The generator preserves the identity, $D(I)=0$, so $e^{tD}(I)=I$.

Let $\sigma=\sigma^*>0$ be a dimensionless density matrix on $\mathcal H$, so $\operatorname{Tr}\sigma=1$. Define

$$\langle A,B\rangle_\sigma:=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma B^*A),\qquad \|A\|_\sigma:=\langle A,A\rangle_\sigma^{1/2}.$$

This inner product is linear in its first variable. It is positive definite because $\sigma>0$. The data satisfy **the specified finite GNS detailed-balance convention** when $[H_{\rm s},\sigma]=0$ and $D$ is self-adjoint for this inner product, meaning $\langle D(A),B\rangle_\sigma=\langle A,D(B)\rangle_\sigma$ for all $A,B\in M_d(\mathbb C)$. The Hamiltonian part of $G$ is kept separate and is anti-self-adjoint. Quantum detailed-balance conventions vary; in particular, this definition does not identify GNS symmetry with KMS or Kubo–Mori symmetry.

items.title: Faithful scalar-kernel detailed balance gives a relaxation gap

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §1.3.4
Eric A. Carlen and Jan Maas, Gradient flow and entropy inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups with detailed balance, §§2 and 7

items.statement:
Let $d\geq1$, and let $G=K+D$ and the faithful density matrix $\sigma$ satisfy [[def-qsm-dt-gns-detailed-balance]], with $\ker D=\mathbb C I$. Write $\mathcal M_0=\{A\in M_d(\mathbb C):\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma A)=0\}$. If $d>1$, the restriction $D|_{\mathcal M_0}$ has only strictly negative eigenvalues. Define

$$\gamma:=\min\{-\lambda:\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(D|_{\mathcal M_0})\}>0.$$

Then for every $A\in\mathcal M_0$ and $t\geq0$,

$$\|e^{tG}A\|_\sigma\leq e^{-\gamma t}\|A\|_\sigma.$$

For every density matrix $\rho$, let $\rho_t=e^{t\mathcal L}\rho$, where $\mathcal L$ is the Schrödinger trace-dual generator. Then

$$\|\rho_t-\sigma\|_1\leq\|\sigma^{-1/2}(\rho-\sigma)\|_2e^{-\gamma t}.$$

Here $\|X\|_1=\operatorname{Tr}\sqrt{X^*X}$ and $\|X\|_2=(\operatorname{Tr}X^*X)^{1/2}$. For centered $A,B\in\mathcal M_0$, the correlation $t\mapsto\langle e^{tG}A,B\rangle_\sigma$ is absolutely integrable. Also

$$\Gamma(A):=\operatorname{Re}\int_0^\infty\langle e^{tG}A,A\rangle_\sigma\,dt=\operatorname{Re}\langle(-G|_{\mathcal M_0})^{-1}A,A\rangle_\sigma\geq0.$$

For $d=1$, $\mathcal M_0=\{0\}$, $\rho=\sigma$, and all centered and relaxation claims are trivial; no $\gamma$ is defined. The units of $\gamma$ are seconds$^{-1}$. These are finite-dimensional conditional model results; they assert no infinite-dimensional bath limit.

items.title: Connected Gibbs jump generators satisfy detailed balance

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §1.3.4
David Aldous and James Allen Fill, Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, Chapters 2–3
Eric A. Carlen and Jan Maas, Gradient flow and entropy inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups with detailed balance, §2

items.statement:
Let $d\geq2$, let $E=\{1,\ldots,d\}$, let $E_a\in\mathbb R$ be finite energies in joules, and let $\beta>0$ have units joule$^{-1}$. Define

$$Z_\beta:=\sum_{a\in E}e^{-\beta E_a},\qquad \pi_a:=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta E_a}.$$

For each $a\ne b$, let $w_{ab}\geq0$ be a rate in seconds$^{-1}$ satisfying Gibbs detailed balance $\pi_aw_{ab}=\pi_bw_{ba}$, and assume the undirected graph with edge $\{a,b\}$ whenever $w_{ab}>0$ is connected. On $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^d$, fix an orthonormal energy basis $(|a\rangle)$, set $H_{\rm s}=\sum_aE_a|a\rangle\langle a|$, and define $L_{ab}=\sqrt{w_{ab}}|b\rangle\langle a|$ for $a\ne b$. Fix $\hbar>0$ in joule-seconds. For real functions $f,g:E\to\mathbb R$, define $\langle f,g\rangle_\pi:=\sum_a\pi_af_ag_a$, and define the row-generator action on column observables by $(Wf)_a:=\sum_{b\ne a}w_{ab}(f_b-f_a)$. Let

$$\sigma:=\sum_a\pi_a|a\rangle\langle a|,\qquad r_a:=\sum_{b\ne a}w_{ab}.$$

Use the finite GKSL generator with Hamiltonian $H_{\rm s}$ and the jump matrices $L_{ab}$. Its observable dissipator $D$ is self-adjoint for the $\sigma$-GNS inner product of [[def-qsm-dt-gns-detailed-balance]], $H_{\rm s}$ commutes with $\sigma$, and $\ker D=\mathbb C I$. On diagonal observables, $W$ is self-adjoint on $L^2(E,\pi)$ with constants as its kernel; for $d\geq2$ its restriction to $\pi^\perp:=\{f:E\to\mathbb R:\sum_a\pi_af_a=0\}$ has a positive spectral gap $\gamma_{\rm cl}$. Thus the generator satisfies the specified finite GNS detailed-balance convention and the generic gap conclusion of [[thm-qsm-dt-detailed-balance-gap]] applies. This claim does not assert a microscopic bath limit.

items.title: Specified energy-jump instrument realizes a finite chain

references.title: M. B. Plenio and P. L. Knight, The quantum-jump approach to dissipative dynamics in quantum optics, §IV.1 “Quantum jumps” and §IV.3 “Simulation of single trajectories”, equations 120–133
David Aldous and James Allen Fill, Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, Chapter 2 §2.1.2

items.statement:
Use the finite energy basis, energies $E_a$, rates $w_{ab}$, Hamiltonian $H_{\rm s}$, and jump matrices $L_{ab}=\sqrt{w_{ab}}|b\rangle\langle a|$ of [[thm-qsm-dt-gibbs-jump]]. Define $R:=\sum_{a\ne b}L_{ab}^*L_{ab}=\sum_a r_a|a\rangle\langle a|$ and the no-click matrix $K:=-iH_{\rm s}/\hbar-R/2$. The **specified energy-resolved instrument** has the following outcomes:

1. If the current state is the energy eigenstate $|a\rangle$, then during a no-click interval of length $t$ the unnormalized state is $e^{tK}|a\rangle$.
2. In an infinitesimal interval $dt$, the outcome labelled $a\to b$ has jump operation $\sqrt{dt}\,L_{ab}$ and probability $dt\,\langle a|L_{ab}^*L_{ab}|a\rangle+o(dt)$. Its normalized post-click state is $L_{ab}|a\rangle/\|L_{ab}|a\rangle\|=|b\rangle$.
3. The no-click operation over $dt$ is $M_0(dt)=I+Kdt+o(dt)$. Since $K^*+K=-R$ and $\sum_{a\ne b}L_{ab}^*L_{ab}=R$, the no-click and jump effects sum to $I+o(dt)$.
4. After each recorded jump, repeat the same rule from the new energy label.

The output path records the current label $a(t)\in E$. This is one selected instrument model; the one-time GKSL semigroup alone does not specify a unique record process.

items.title: Gibbs jump commuting relative entropy production

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §1.3.4
Eric A. Carlen and Jan Maas, Gradient flow and entropy inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups with detailed balance, §2

items.statement:
Use the finite connected Gibbs jump model of [[thm-qsm-dt-gibbs-jump]]. For a diagonal density $\rho_t=\sum_a p_a(t)|a\rangle\langle a|$, the populations satisfy $p'_a=\sum_{b\ne a}(p_bw_{ba}-p_aw_{ab})$. Define the dimensionless classical relative entropy

$$K(p\mid\pi):=\sum_{a\in E}p_a\log\frac{p_a}{\pi_a},\qquad 0\log(0/\pi_a):=0,$$

where $\log$ is the natural logarithm. For every $t>0$, $p_a(t)>0$ for all $a$, and

$$\frac{d}{dt}K(p_t\mid\pi)=-\frac12\sum_{\substack{a,b\in E\\a\ne b}}\pi_aw_{ab}(u_a-u_b)(\log u_a-\log u_b)\leq0,\qquad u_a:=p_a/\pi_a.$$

Equality in this derivative holds exactly when $p_t=\pi$. For any initial probability vector, including one with zero entries, $t\mapsto K(p_t\mid\pi)$ is continuous at $t=0$ and nonincreasing on $[0,\infty)$. This is a finite commuting-state statement; it asserts no entropy-production theorem for noncommuting densities.

items.title: Gap-controlled correlation resolvent and positive coefficients

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §1.3.4
Eric A. Carlen and Jan Maas, Gradient flow and entropy inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups with detailed balance, §§2 and 7

items.statement:
Assume the finite GNS detailed-balance hypotheses, $d>1$, and the positive gap $\gamma$ of [[thm-qsm-dt-detailed-balance-gap]]. For centered $A,B\in\mathcal M_0$, define $C_{A,B}(t):=\langle e^{tG}A,B\rangle_\sigma$. Then

$$|C_{A,B}(t)|\leq e^{-\gamma t}\|A\|_\sigma\|B\|_\sigma,\qquad t\geq0,$$

so the correlation is absolutely integrable and

$$\int_0^\infty C_{A,B}(t)\,dt=\left\langle(-G|_{\mathcal M_0})^{-1}A,B\right\rangle_\sigma.$$

For centered $A$, the real coefficient

$$\Gamma(A):=\operatorname{Re}\int_0^\infty\langle e^{tG}A,A\rangle_\sigma\,dt$$

is nonnegative. Its real polarization on any finite list of Hermitian centered observables is a positive-semidefinite real symmetric correlation-integral matrix. No mixing, central-limit theorem, or infinite-volume transport claim follows.

items.title: Fixed-dissipator finite response and integrable kernel

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §§1.3.4 and 1.4.2
Eric A. Carlen and Jan Maas, Gradient flow and entropy inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups with detailed balance, §2

items.statement:
Let $\mathcal L_0$ be the finite Schrödinger generator trace-dual to $G$ in [[def-qsm-dt-gns-detailed-balance]], and assume the gap hypotheses of [[thm-qsm-dt-detailed-balance-gap]] with $d>1$. Let $A\in M_d(\mathbb C)$, $B=B^*\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ be dimensionless observables, and let $h:[0,T]\to\mathbb R$ be continuous with units joules. For dimensionless $\epsilon\in\mathbb R$, perturb only the Hamiltonian by $H_\epsilon(t)=H_{\rm s}-\epsilon h(t)B$; hold the dissipator fixed. Let $\rho^\epsilon_t$ be the unique state solution with $\rho^\epsilon_0=\sigma$, supplied by [[thm-qsm-dt-time-dependent-gksl]].

Define $A_0:=A-\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma A)I$ and, for $\tau\geq0$,

$$R_{AB}(\tau):=\frac{i}{\hbar}\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sigma[e^{\tau G}A_0,B]\right).$$

Then, on every finite interval $[0,T]$, the derivative at $\epsilon=0$ exists and

$$\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}\operatorname{Tr}(\rho^\epsilon_tA)\right|_{\epsilon=0}=\int_0^t h(s)R_{AB}(t-s)\,ds.$$

The kernel is absolutely integrable on $[0,\infty)$. If $\mu$ is the smallest eigenvalue of $\sigma$, then

$$|R_{AB}(\tau)|\leq\frac{2\|B\|_\infty}{\hbar\sqrt{\mu}}\,e^{-\gamma\tau}\|A_0\|_\sigma.$$

This is an open-system model response with a fixed dissipator. It does not assert that the driven stationary state is the Gibbs state of $H_{\rm s}-\epsilon hB$.

items.title: Specified effective GKSL bath and instrument assumption
items.physical_scope: For a finite-dimensional subsystem represented by H=C^d (d>=1), the chosen thermal GKSL state law and energy-resolved instrument apply physically only on the declared finite interval [0,t_res], where t_res>0 is in seconds. All-time limits are mathematical continuations of the same fixed generator and instrument, with no physical-applicability claim beyond t_res. No microscopic bath limit, calibrated rate, or reported measurement is asserted.

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §§1.3.4 and 1.5.3
M. B. Plenio and P. L. Knight, The quantum-jump approach to dissipative dynamics in quantum optics, §IV.1 “Quantum jumps” and §IV.3 “Simulation of single trajectories”

items.statement:
Let $d\geq1$ be finite and let the modeled subsystem Hilbert space be $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^d$. A state is a dimensionless matrix $\rho=\rho^*\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ such that $x^*\rho x\geq0$ for every $x\in\mathbb C^d$ and $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. An initial preparation is a chosen state $\rho_0$. Let $H_{\rm s}=H_{\rm s}^*\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ have units joules, let $\hbar>0$ have units joule-seconds, and let $L_1,\ldots,L_m\in M_d(\mathbb C)$, $m\geq0$ finite, have units seconds$^{-1/2}$. We adopt the time-independent finite GKSL generator of [[def-qsm-dt-gksl-definition]],

$$\mathcal L(X)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}[H_{\rm s},X]+\sum_{j=1}^{m}\left(L_jXL_j^*-\frac12\{L_j^*L_j,X\}\right),$$

where $[U,V]=UV-VU$ and $\{U,V\}=UV+VU$. The exact state law is

$$\frac{d}{dt}\rho_t=\mathcal L(\rho_t),\qquad \rho_{t=0}=\rho_0,\qquad \rho_t=e^{t\mathcal L}\rho_0,\qquad 0\leq t\leq t_{\rm res}.$$

Here $t_{\rm res}\in(0,\infty)$ is the finite resolved duration, in seconds, adopted for this model. For mathematical long-time calculations, the same constant generator defines the continuation $e^{t\mathcal L}\rho_0$ for every $t\geq0$; this continuation makes no physical-applicability claim for $t>t_{\rm res}$. By [[thm-qsm-dt-gksl-sufficient]] it is a density-state evolution on that mathematical continuation as well.

Let $k_{\rm B}>0$ denote Boltzmann's constant, with SI units joules per kelvin; it converts absolute temperature to an inverse-energy parameter. Let $T_{\rm bath}>0$ be the adopted absolute temperature parameter in kelvins and set $\beta:=(k_{\rm B}T_{\rm bath})^{-1}$, with units joules$^{-1}$. The temperature and rates are model inputs here; no measured calibration is asserted. The temperature parameter alone imposes no detailed-balance condition on an arbitrary choice of $L_j$. When the generator is specialized to the connected Gibbs-jump model, its energies, $\beta$, and rates must satisfy the hypotheses in [[thm-qsm-dt-gibbs-jump]].

Within this effective formulation, the dimension $d$, preparation $\rho_0$, general coefficient matrices $H_{\rm s}$ and $L_j$, positive constants $\hbar$ and $k_{\rm B}$, temperature $T_{\rm bath}$, and resolved duration $t_{\rm res}$ are primitive, adopted model inputs with the types and units stated above; none is derived here from a microscopic reservoir or inferred from a measurement. This status is local to this formulation, not a claim that each is fundamental in every physical theory. The space $\mathbb C^d$, inverse-energy parameter $\beta$, generator $\mathcal L$, and state family $\rho_t$ are derived by their displayed constructions once those inputs and the physical state-law postulate are fixed. The selected Hermitian observable $A$ and its unit assignment are additional adopted observable data; its expectation is derived by the trace formula below.

In the connected Gibbs-jump parameterization, the orthonormal energy basis, real level energies $E_a$ in joules, and rates $w_{ab}\geq0$ in seconds$^{-1}$ are instead the adopted primitive spectral and rate data, subject to the Gibbs-balance and connectivity hypotheses of [[thm-qsm-dt-gibbs-jump]]. In that parameterization the operator coefficients are derived as $H_{\rm s}=\sum_a E_a|a\rangle\langle a|$ and $L_{ab}=\sqrt{w_{ab}}|b\rangle\langle a|$; they replace, rather than supplement, the independent general matrix choices above. The Gibbs weights $\pi_a=e^{-\beta E_a}/\sum_b e^{-\beta E_b}$ are derived, while the energy-resolved instrument remains a separate adopted assumption. In particular, neither the temperature nor the Gibbs-balance relation derives the numerical rates.

For that Gibbs-jump specialization, record predictions additionally adopt the particular ideal energy-resolved instrument defined in [[def-qsm-dt-monitored-chain]], and only on $0\leq t\leq t_{\rm res}$ as a physical model. Its law for all $t\geq0$ is used only as a mathematical continuation when deriving a long-time coefficient. A one-time channel family alone does not select this record law. Full [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is retained as the formal set-theoretic premise in the monitored-chain supplier's construction of the joint path law; it is not a physical postulate about nature. A selected observable is represented by a Hermitian matrix $A\in M_d(\mathbb C)$ with its assigned physical units, and its model expectation $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_tA)$ has those same units; no measurement outcome is reported.

items.title: Stationary monitored-chain transport variance coefficient

references.title: David Aldous and James Allen Fill, Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, Chapters 2–3
M. B. Plenio and P. L. Knight, The quantum-jump approach to dissipative dynamics in quantum optics, §IV.1 “Quantum jumps” and §IV.3 “Simulation of single trajectories”

items.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice and the connected finite Gibbs jump data of [[thm-qsm-dt-gibbs-jump]]. Use the energy-resolved record path supplied by [[def-qsm-dt-monitored-chain]], initialized with law $\pi$. Let $v:E\to\mathbb R$ be a real velocity observable with units metres per second and $\pi(v):=\sum_a\pi_av_a=0$. Define the record displacement

$$Y_T:=\int_0^T v_{a(s)}\,ds,\qquad C_v(s):=\langle v,e^{sW}v\rangle_\pi,$$

where $Wf(a)=\sum_{b\ne a}w_{ab}(f_b-f_a)$, $\langle f,g\rangle_\pi=\sum_a\pi_a f_ag_a$, and $\pi^\perp:=\{f:E\to\mathbb R:\sum_a\pi_af_a=0\}$. Then for every $T\geq0$,

$$\mathbb E_\pi[Y_T]=0,\qquad \operatorname{Var}_\pi(Y_T)=2\int_0^T(T-s)C_v(s)\,ds.$$

If $\gamma_{\rm cl}>0$ is the reversible spectral gap of $W$ on $\pi$-centered functions, then $|C_v(s)|\leq e^{-\gamma_{\rm cl}s}\sum_a\pi_av_a^2$, and

$$D_{\rm rec}:=\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{Var}_\pi(Y_T)}{2T}=\int_0^\infty C_v(s)\,ds=\langle(-W|_{\pi^\perp})^{-1}v,v\rangle_\pi\geq0.$$

The units of $D_{\rm rec}$ are square metres per second. This proves a variance coefficient for the selected finite record model; it does not prove a central-limit theorem or a generic quantum transport law.

items.title: Conditional specified thermal bath relaxation
items.physical_scope: Conditional predictions for the specified finite connected Gibbs-jump GKSL model, physically applicable only on the postulate's finite interval [0,t_res]. The all-time exponential estimate and qubit formulas are proved for the mathematical continuation of the fixed generator; no physical applicability for t>t_res, measured rates, microscopic bath limit, or universal thermalization law is claimed.

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §§1.3.4 and 1.5.3
Eric A. Carlen and Jan Maas, Gradient flow and entropy inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups with detailed balance, §2

items.statement:
Assume full AC, the adopted finite effective-bath model [[post-qsm-dt-effective-bath]] on its physical interval $0\leq t\leq t_{\rm res}$, and the connected finite Gibbs-jump hypotheses of [[thm-qsm-dt-gibbs-jump]]. For an initial density $\rho$, let $\rho_t=e^{t\mathcal L}\rho$ denote the mathematical all-time continuation of the fixed finite Schrödinger generator, and let $\sigma=Z_\beta^{-1}e^{-\beta H_{\rm s}}$. If $d>1$, the finite detailed-balance gap $\gamma>0$ gives the conditional model prediction for every $t\geq0$ in that continuation

$$\|\rho_t-\sigma\|_1\leq\|\sigma^{-1/2}(\rho-\sigma)\|_2e^{-\gamma t}.$$

Under the adopted physical model this bound is applicable only for $0\leq t\leq t_{\rm res}$; its all-time form is a mathematical consequence of continuing the same fixed generator, not a claim about physical evolution for $t>t_{\rm res}$.

For the two-level specialization, let $H_{\rm s}=\Delta Z/2$, $\Delta>0$ joules, $Z=|0\rangle\langle0|-|1\rangle\langle1|$, and $X=|0\rangle\langle1|+|1\rangle\langle0|$, $Y=-i|0\rangle\langle1|+i|1\rangle\langle0|$. Adopt downward jump $\sqrt a\,|1\rangle\langle0|$ with $a>0$ seconds$^{-1}$, upward jump $\sqrt b\,|0\rangle\langle1|$ with $b/a=e^{-\beta\Delta}$, and optionally a dephasing jump $\sqrt{\gamma_\phi/2}\,Z$ with $\gamma_\phi\geq0$ seconds$^{-1}$. Put

$$\omega:=\Delta/\hbar,\quad \gamma_1:=a+b,\quad \gamma_2:=\frac{a+b}{2}+\gamma_\phi,\quad z_{\rm eq}:=\frac{b-a}{a+b}=-\tanh(\beta\Delta/2).$$

For every $t\geq0$ in the mathematical continuation, the exact model expectations and coherence satisfy

$$\langle Z\rangle_t=z_{\rm eq}+e^{-\gamma_1t}(\langle Z\rangle_0-z_{\rm eq}),\qquad \rho_{01}(t)=e^{-(\gamma_2+i\omega)t}\rho_{01}(0).$$

Equivalently, $e^{tG}X=e^{-\gamma_2t}(X\cos\omega t-Y\sin\omega t)$ and $e^{tG}Z=z_{\rm eq}I+e^{-\gamma_1t}(Z-z_{\rm eq}I)$. For $d=1$, $\rho=\sigma$ and relaxation is trivial. These are conditional model deductions, not experimental findings or claims that a physical bath realizes the postulate.

The qubit formulas above are stated for the mathematical continuation; their physical model applicability is limited to $0\leq t\leq t_{\rm res}$.

items.title: Conditional instrument-record diffusion coefficient
items.physical_scope: Conditional finite-model prediction for the specified ideal energy-resolved monitoring instrument, Gibbs initial law, and assigned pointer velocities. Physical applicability is limited to the postulate's finite interval [0,t_res]; the T->infinity coefficient is mathematical for the continued finite-rate model. It is not a measured spatial diffusion coefficient or a generic quantum hydrodynamic limit.

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §1.3.4
M. B. Plenio and P. L. Knight, The quantum-jump approach to dissipative dynamics in quantum optics, §IV.1 “Quantum jumps” and §IV.3 “Simulation of single trajectories”

items.statement:
Assume full AC, [[post-qsm-dt-effective-bath]], and the finite connected Gibbs-jump model with its selected energy-resolved instrument. Prepare the system with diagonal Gibbs law $\pi$. Assign a real pointer velocity $v_a$ in metres per second to each recorded energy label, with $\sum_a\pi_av_a=0$, and define the model record displacement $Y_T=\int_0^T v_{a(s)}\,ds$. The postulate's physical applicability is limited to $0\leq t\leq t_{\rm res}$. For formulas at arbitrary $T\geq0$ and their limit, continue the same finite-rate chain as an idealized mathematical model; this gives no physical-applicability claim for $T>t_{\rm res}$. Thus the displayed formula is a conditional physical-model prediction for $0\leq T\leq t_{\rm res}$ and a mathematical model identity for all $T\geq0$ in the continuation:

$$\mathbb E_\pi[Y_T]=0,\qquad \operatorname{Var}_\pi(Y_T)=2\int_0^T(T-s)C_v(s)\,ds,$$

where $C_v(s)=\sum_a\pi_av_a(e^{sW}v)_a$. The limit

$$D_{\rm rec}:=\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{Var}_\pi(Y_T)}{2T}=\int_0^\infty C_v(s)\,ds=\langle(-W|_{\pi^\perp})^{-1}v,v\rangle_\pi\geq0$$

exists and has units square metres per second. This long-time limit is a derived coefficient of the idealized mathematical continuation. It is not a measurement of a system's position, a calibrated material coefficient, or evidence that the microscopic bath obeys the effective model.

title: Specified finite GNS detailed balance — Examples

items.title: Solved Gibbs qubit relaxation and finite response coefficients

references.title: Robert Alicki and Karl Lendi, Quantum Dynamical Semigroups and Applications, Lecture Notes in Physics 717, §§1.5.3 and 1.3.4
Eric A. Carlen and Jan Maas, Gradient flow and entropy inequalities for quantum Markov semigroups with detailed balance, §2

items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^2$, $H_{\rm s}=\Delta Z/2$ with $\Delta>0$ joules, $Z=|0\rangle\langle0|-|1\rangle\langle1|$, $X=|0\rangle\langle1|+|1\rangle\langle0|$, and $Y=-i|0\rangle\langle1|+i|1\rangle\langle0|$. Take downward rate $a>0$, upward rate $b>0$, $b/a=e^{-\beta\Delta}$, and optional dephasing rate $\gamma_\phi\geq0$. Here $\beta>0$ is in joules$^{-1}$, $\hbar$ is in joule-seconds, and $a,b,\gamma_\phi$ are in seconds$^{-1}$. Use the finite GKSL generator of [[def-qsm-dt-gns-detailed-balance]] with Hamiltonian $H_{\rm s}$ and exactly the jumps $L_\downarrow=\sqrt a\,|1\rangle\langle0|$, $L_\uparrow=\sqrt b\,|0\rangle\langle1|$, and $L_\phi=\sqrt{\gamma_\phi/2}\,Z$. Thus the additional dephasing dissipator, on either states or observables, is $D_\phi(A)=(\gamma_\phi/2)(ZAZ-A)$; when $\gamma_\phi=0$ this jump is zero. Let $\gamma_1=a+b$, $\gamma_2=(a+b)/2+\gamma_\phi$, $\omega=\Delta/\hbar$, and $z_{\rm eq}=-\tanh(\beta\Delta/2)$. Set $\sigma=(I+z_{\rm eq}Z)/2$. Define the centered correlations

$$C_{XX}(t):=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma e^{tG}(X)X),\qquad C_{ZZ}(t):=\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma e^{tG}(Z-z_{\rm eq}I)(Z-z_{\rm eq}I)).$$

Then

$$C_{XX}(t)=e^{-\gamma_2t}\left(\cos(\omega t)-i\tanh(\beta\Delta/2)\sin(\omega t)\right),\qquad C_{ZZ}(t)=(1-z_{\rm eq}^2)e^{-\gamma_1t}.$$

The real correlation-integral coefficients are

$$\Gamma_X=\frac{\gamma_2}{\gamma_2^2+\omega^2},\qquad \Gamma_Z=\frac{1-z_{\rm eq}^2}{\gamma_1}.$$

Under the fixed-dissipator perturbation $H_\epsilon(t)=H_{\rm s}-\epsilon h(t)X$, define $\chi_{\rm open}(0):=\int_0^\infty R_{XX}(t)\,dt$. The open response kernel and its zero-frequency integral are

$$R_{XX}(t)=\frac{2}{\hbar}\tanh(\beta\Delta/2)e^{-\gamma_2t}\sin(\omega t),\qquad \chi_{\rm open}(0)=\frac{2\tanh(\beta\Delta/2)\,\omega}{\hbar(\gamma_2^2+\omega^2)}.$$

For $q\in\mathbb R$ measured in joules, define $H(q):=H_{\rm s}-qX$ and $\sigma_q:=e^{-\beta H(q)}/\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta H(q)})$. The static Gibbs susceptibility for this family is

$$\chi_{\rm Gibbs}(0):=\left.\frac{d}{dq}\operatorname{Tr}(\sigma_qX)\right|_{q=0}=\frac{2}{\hbar\omega}\tanh(\beta\Delta/2).$$

Thus $\chi_{\rm open}(0)$ and $\chi_{\rm Gibbs}(0)$ differ for positive $\gamma_2$; the model has a fixed dissipator, so its zero-frequency response is not the derivative of the instantaneous Gibbs preparation.

items.title: Exact centered qubit-record displacement variance

references.title: David Aldous and James Allen Fill, Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, Chapters 2–3
M. B. Plenio and P. L. Knight, The quantum-jump approach to dissipative dynamics in quantum optics, §IV.1 “Quantum jumps” and §IV.3 “Simulation of single trajectories”

items.statement:
Assume full AC and initialize the selected energy-resolved record with the Gibbs law $\pi$. Use the two energy states $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$ of [[thm-qsm-dt-gibbs-jump]] with energies $E_0=\Delta/2$ and $E_1=-\Delta/2$, where $\Delta>0$ is in joules and $\beta>0$ is in joules$^{-1}$. Let $a>0$ be the rate from $0\to1$ and $b>0$ the rate from $1\to0$, both in seconds$^{-1}$, with $b/a=e^{-\beta\Delta}$. The stationary mean is $z_{\rm eq}:=(b-a)/(a+b)$. Write $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$ and let $v_0$ be a speed scale in metres per second; assign centered pointer velocities $v_a=v_0(Z_{aa}-z_{\rm eq})$. The monitored record displacement $Y_T=\int_0^T v_{a(s)}ds$ has

$$C_v(s)=v_0^2(1-z_{\rm eq}^2)e^{-(a+b)s},$$

and exact variance

$$\operatorname{Var}(Y_T)=2v_0^2(1-z_{\rm eq}^2)\left[\frac{T}{a+b}-\frac{1-e^{-(a+b)T}}{(a+b)^2}\right].$$

Consequently

$$\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{\operatorname{Var}(Y_T)}{2T}=\frac{v_0^2(1-z_{\rm eq}^2)}{a+b}.$$

This is a variance of the selected classical record with units of squared metres. The record is not asserted to be a continuous quantum position or an experimental velocity.
